theme: T2 Trust in AI for SE
title: On the Need to Rethink Trust in AI Assistants for Software Development: A Critical Review
authors: Sebastian Baltes; Timo Speith; Brenda Chiteri; Seyedmoein Mohsenimofidi; Shalini Chakraborty; Daniel Buschek
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
objective: Critically review how trust is conceptualised in SE research on AI assistants.
methodology: Review of trust foundations and conceptualisations across SE, HCI and IS.
main_findings: SE research often equates trust with acceptance of generated content, which does not capture the construct; recommends adopting established trust models.
future_research: Use established trust models and measures.
relevance_to_trustcode: Critical for TrustCode measurement design: measure trust (attitude), reliance (behaviour) and calibration separately — never use acceptance rate as trust.

theme: T2 Trust in AI for SE
title: Investigating and Designing for Trust in AI-powered Code Generation Tools
authors: Ruotong Wang; Ruijia Cheng; Denae Ford; Thomas Zimmermann
venue: The 2024 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency
objective: Understand how developers evaluate trustworthiness of AI code generation tools and design for trust.
methodology: Study 1 interviews; Study 2 design probe of suggestion quality indicators, usage stats, control mechanisms.
main_findings: Trust is rooted in perceived ability, integrity, benevolence and is situational; current tools lack affordances to evaluate trustworthiness efficiently.
limitations_reviewer_assessed: Qualitative; design concepts not evaluated behaviourally.
relevance_to_trustcode: Directly motivates TrustCode's evidence affordances; TrustCode operationalises and tests them.

title: Fostering Appropriate Reliance on Large Language Models: The Role of Explanations, Sources, and Inconsistencies
authors: Sunnie S. Y. Kim; Jennifer Wortman Vaughan; Q. Vera Liao; Tania Lombrozo; Olga Russakovsky
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
objective: Identify LLM response features that shape reliance.
methodology: Think-aloud study then pre-registered controlled experiment.
main_findings: Explanations increased reliance on both correct and incorrect answers; sources and inconsistencies reduced reliance on incorrect answers.
relevance_to_trustcode: Strong analogue: checkable sources (≈ tool evidence) help; explanations alone hurt. Underpins H1/H2.

title: Explanations Can Reduce Overreliance on AI Systems During Decision-Making
authors: Helena Vasconcelos; Matthew Jörke; Madeleine Grunde-McLaughlin; Tobias Gerstenberg; Michael S. Bernstein; Ranjay Krishna
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
objective: Explain when explanations reduce overreliance.
methodology: Cost-benefit framework; 5 studies with a maze task.
main_findings: People strategically decide whether to engage with explanations; explanations reduce overreliance when they lower the cost of verifying the AI.
relevance_to_trustcode: Theoretical basis for TrustCode: evidence should reduce verification cost, not merely add text.

title: Does the Whole Exceed its Parts? The Effect of AI Explanations on Complementary Team Performance
authors: Gagan Bansal; Tongshuang Wu; Joyce Zhou; Raymond Fok; Besmira Nushi; Ece Kamar; Marco Tulio Ribeiro; Daniel Weld
venue: Proceedings of the 2021 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
objective: Test whether AI explanations produce complementary human-AI team performance.
methodology: Mixed-method user studies on three datasets.
main_findings: Explanations increased the chance that humans accept AI recommendations regardless of correctness; they did not increase complementary performance.
relevance_to_trustcode: Core risk for TrustCode: fluent LLM explanations may increase overreliance — motivates evidence-first design.

title: Trust-Calibrated Code Review: A Participatory Design Study of Review Workflows for LLM-Generated Multi-File Changes
authors: Lo Gullstrand Heander; Agnia Sergeyuk; Ilya Zakharov; Emma Söderberg; Nikita Mukhortov
venue: arXiv preprint
objective: Understand challenges of reviewing LLM-generated multi-file changes and envision review workflows.
methodology: Participatory design (double-diamond) with JetBrains; prototype evaluated by survey.
main_findings: Participants framed review of LLM changes as a trust-calibration problem; proposed 3-level workflow and 7 constructs (e.g., risk-per-line, risk-per-file, judge, security cage); survey means 3.50-3.91/5; 63% expected reduced review effort.
limitations_reviewer_assessed: Outcomes are self-reported expectations; no controlled measurement of decision accuracy or calibration; preprint (submitted to ESEM).
future_research: Implementation and empirical evaluation of the constructs.
relevance_to_trustcode: Strong independent confirmation that trust calibration is the core problem; leaves behavioural evaluation open, which TrustCode targets.

title: Evaluating the Impact of Explainable AI on Trust in AI-Assisted Code Review
authors: Zhenhan Gao; Marvin Muñoz Barón; Umm-e Habiba; Daniel Graziotin; Stefan Wagner
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering
objective: Study how explainable AI affects developer trust in AI-assisted code review.
methodology: Within-subjects study; three LLM code-review systems: A detailed explanation+feedback, B feedback only, C no explanation; real code change requests.
main_findings: Explanation level significantly changed perceived trust and agreement; full explanations gave highest perceived trust (M=3.99/5) but not highest agreement (B: 89.22%); no significant effect on time.
limitations_reviewer_assessed: Explanations are LLM-generated, not tool-verified evidence; abstract does not report correctness-conditioned reliance (agreement vs ground truth).
future_research: Design of trustworthy AI code review systems.
relevance_to_trustcode: Closest controlled study. TrustCode differs by (i) tool-grounded evidence with epistemic status, (ii) ground-truth benchmark enabling calibration metrics, (iii) generated code rather than review comments.

title: Validating AI-Generated Code with Live Programming
authors: Kasra Ferdowsi; Ruanqianqian (Lisa) Huang; Michael B. James; Nadia Polikarpova; Sorin Lerner
venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
objective: Test whether Live Programming (continuous display of runtime values) helps programmers validate AI-generated code.
methodology: Built a Python editor combining an AI assistant with an LP environment; between-subjects lab study.
main_findings: Lowering the cost of validation-by-execution with LP mitigated over- and under-reliance on AI-generated programs and reduced validation cognitive load for some task types.
limitations_reviewer_assessed: Small sample (N=17); runtime-value evidence only (no static/security analysis); short self-contained tasks.
future_research: Other forms of low-cost validation evidence; larger and more realistic tasks.
relevance_to_trustcode: Closest prior evidence that making verification cheaper changes reliance. TrustCode must differentiate: multi-source tool evidence (tests, static, security) with explicit epistemic status, and calibration measured against ground truth.

title: Generation Probabilities Are Not Enough: Uncertainty Highlighting in AI Code Completions
authors: Helena Vasconcelos; Gagan Bansal; Adam Fourney; Q. Vera Liao; Jennifer Wortman Vaughan
venue: ACM Transactions on Computer-Human Interaction
objective: Evaluate whether highlighting uncertain tokens in AI code completions helps programmers find errors.
methodology: Mixed-methods study comparing no highlighting, low-generation-probability highlighting, and predicted-edit-likelihood highlighting.
main_findings: Highlighting tokens most likely to be edited led to faster completion and more targeted edits and was preferred; highlighting by raw generation probability was not effective.
limitations_reviewer_assessed: Model-internal uncertainty signal, not verification evidence; completion setting.
future_research: Better uncertainty signals for code; combining with other evidence.
relevance_to_trustcode: Shows that a naive confidence signal (token probability) does not help — supports TrustCode's premise that confidence scores alone are insufficient.

theme: T5 Quality & security of AI code
title: Do Users Write More Insecure Code with AI Assistants?
authors: Neil Perry; Megha Srivastava; Deepak Kumar; Dan Boneh
venue: Proceedings of the 2023 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security
objective: Examine whether AI assistants lead users to write insecure code.
main_findings: Participants with AI access wrote significantly less secure code and were more likely to believe their code was secure.
relevance_to_trustcode: Direct evidence of miscalibrated confidence with AI code — the problem TrustCode targets.

title: TARS: A Theory-of-Mind Agent for Personalized In-IDE Code Comprehension
authors: Leopoldo Todisco; Antonio Della Porta; Stefano Lambiase; Fabio Palomba
venue: arXiv preprint
objective: Personalised in-IDE code comprehension via a Theory-of-Mind LLM agent.
methodology: VS Code agent profiling expertise, role, style; RAG grounding; controlled experiment.
main_findings: TARS users were 26% faster, reported lower cognitive load, and found explanations adapted to their profiles.
limitations_reviewer_assessed: Small sample; comprehension task, not verification of AI code; trust calibration not measured; tool-demo track.
relevance_to_trustcode: Most direct prior art for expertise-adaptive explanations in VS Code — TrustCode's adaptation is NOT novel by itself; novelty must come from holding evidence invariant and measuring effect on calibrated reliance.

title: When Help Hurts: Verification Load and Fatigue with AI Coding Assistants
authors: Guangrui Fan; Dandan Liu; Lihu Pan; Rui Zhang
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
objective: Study verification load and fatigue with AI coding assistants across interaction modes.
methodology: See paper (abstract not retrieved; publisher page blocked).
main_findings: Per search snippet only: novices benefited from a Structured mode at mid complexity (lower TLX, higher correctness) while experienced developers favoured Inline on simple and Chat on complex work. MUST read full text before citing.
relevance_to_trustcode: Potentially the closest evidence that expertise moderates verification outcomes; key paper to read in full.

title: Appropriate Reliance on AI Advice: Conceptualization and the Effect of Explanations
authors: Max Schemmer; Niklas Kuehl; Carina Benz; Andrea Bartos; Gerhard Satzger
venue: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces
objective: Conceptualise and measure appropriate reliance.
main_findings: Proposes Appropriateness of Reliance (AoR), a two-dimensional measure (relative AI reliance, relative self-reliance).
relevance_to_trustcode: Candidate primary operationalisation of calibrated reliance in TrustCode.

title: Complacency and Bias in Human Use of Automation: An Attentional Integration
authors: Raja Parasuraman; Dietrich H. Manzey
venue: Human Factors: The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society
objective: Integrate automation complacency and bias.
main_findings: Automation bias and complacency arise from attentional processes and occur in experts as well as novices.
relevance_to_trustcode: Predicts the 'all checks passed' complacency risk tested by TrustCode H3.

title: Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance
authors: John D. Lee; Katrina A. See
venue: Human Factors: The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society
objective: Theory of trust in automation.
main_findings: Defines appropriate reliance and calibration (trust matching capability), resolution and specificity.
relevance_to_trustcode: Primary theoretical foundation.

theme: T1 Interaction with AI code assistants
title: Humans are Missing from AI Coding Agent Research
authors: Zora Z. Wang; John Yang; Kilian Lieret; Alexa Tartaglini; Valerie Chen; Yuxiang Wei; Zijian Wang; Lingming Zhang; Karthik Narasimhan; Ludwig Schmidt; Graham Neubig; Daniel Fried; Diyi Yang
venue: arXiv preprint
objective: Argue for human-centred coding agents.
main_findings: Bottleneck shifts to supervision and trust; identifies task alignment, verifiability, steerability, adaptability; calls for verification mechanisms and measures of interaction quality.
relevance_to_trustcode: Explicit call for exactly the verifiability + adaptability measurement TrustCode targets.

theme: T1 Interaction with AI code assistants
title: Reading Between the Lines: Modeling User Behavior and Costs in AI-Assisted Programming
authors: Hussein Mozannar; Gagan Bansal; Adam Fourney; Eric Horvitz
venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
objective: Model programmer activities and time costs with Copilot.
methodology: CUPS taxonomy; retrospective labelling of sessions.
main_findings: Revealed inefficiencies and time costs, notably time spent verifying suggestions.
relevance_to_trustcode: Quantifies verification cost — motivates efficiency metric.

theme: T1 Interaction with AI code assistants
title: A Large-Scale Survey on the Usability of AI Programming Assistants: Successes and Challenges
authors: Jenny T. Liang; Chenyang Yang; Brad A. Myers
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/ACM 46th International Conference on Software Engineering
objective: Understand usability challenges of AI programming assistants.
main_findings: Developers often do not accept initial suggestions; key reasons for non-use include code not meeting functional/non-functional requirements and difficulty controlling output.
relevance_to_trustcode: Requirement mismatch motivates TrustCode's contextual (requirement-consistency) check.

theme: T1 Interaction with AI code assistants
title: Grounded Copilot: How Programmers Interact with Code-Generating Models
authors: Shraddha Barke; Michael B. James; Nadia Polikarpova
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages
objective: Grounded theory of programmer interaction with Copilot.
main_findings: Interaction is bimodal: acceleration mode vs exploration mode.
relevance_to_trustcode: Verification needs differ by mode; TrustCode targets deliberate validation (exploration/acceptance) moments.

theme: T1 Interaction with AI code assistants
title: Expectation vs. Experience: Evaluating the Usability of Code Generation Tools Powered by Large Language Models
authors: Priyan Vaithilingam; Tianyi Zhang; Elena L. Glassman
venue: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems Extended Abstracts
objective: Evaluate usability of Copilot in programming workflow.
main_findings: Copilot did not necessarily improve completion time or success; participants struggled to understand, edit and debug generated code.
relevance_to_trustcode: Establishes the verification/understanding burden.

theme: T2 Trust in AI for SE
title: What Needs Attention? Prioritizing Drivers of Developers’ Trust and Adoption of Generative AI
authors: Rudrajit Choudhuri; Bianca Trinkenreich; Rahul Pandita; Eirini Kalliamvakou; Igor Steinmacher; Marco Gerosa; Christopher A. Sanchez; Anita Sarma
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
objective: Model which factors drive developers' trust in and adoption of genAI.
methodology: Theoretical model of trust and adoption (survey-based; see paper).
main_findings: Cognitive style shapes engagement with genAI (e.g., risk-averse developers gate outputs behind tests); tools that ignore individual differences create barriers.
relevance_to_trustcode: Supports adaptation beyond expertise level (cognitive style) — informs TrustCode adaptation design and its limits.

theme: T2 Trust in AI for SE
title: Towards an Appropriate Level of Reliance on AI: A Preliminary Reliance-Control Framework for AI in Software Engineering
authors: Samuel Ferino; Rashina Hoda; John Grundy; Christoph Treude
venue: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on the Foundations of Software Engineering
objective: Propose a framework linking developer control level to over/under-reliance on AI.
main_findings: Preliminary reliance-control framework in which the level of control indicates over- or under-reliance.
future_research: Study control levels supported by LLM tools.
relevance_to_trustcode: Theoretical support for TrustCode's human-control component (RQ4).

theme: T2 Trust in AI for SE
title: Mapping the Trust Terrain: LLMs in Software Engineering - Insights and Perspectives
authors: Dipin Khati; Yijin Liu; David N. Palacio; Yixuan Zhang; Denys Poshyvanyk
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
objective: Clarify concepts of trust in LLMs for SE.
methodology: Systematic review of 18 LLM4SE studies + 70 trust articles; survey of 25 experts.
main_findings: Trust, distrust and trustworthiness lack precise definitions in LLM4SE; trust metrics are undeveloped.
relevance_to_trustcode: Supports the measurement gap TrustCode addresses.

theme: T2 Trust in AI for SE
title: Trust Calibration in IDEs: Paving the Way for Widespread Adoption of AI Refactoring
authors: Markus Borg
venue: arXiv preprint
objective: Position paper on trust calibration for AI refactoring in IDEs.
methodology: Position paper; planned action research at CodeScene.
main_findings: Advocates validating AI refactorings with trustworthy safeguards and designing UI that conveys an appropriate level of trust, grounded in human-factors automation models.
relevance_to_trustcode: Independent articulation of the same design principle (safeguard evidence + calibrated trust UI) — shows the direction is timely, not yet evaluated.

title: To Rely or Not to Rely? Evaluating Interventions for Appropriate Reliance on Large Language Models
authors: Jessica Y Bo; Sophia Wan; Ashton Anderson
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
objective: Benchmark reliance interventions for LLM advice.
main_findings: Interventions reduced over-reliance but generally failed to improve appropriate reliance; people became more confident after wrong reliance decisions.
relevance_to_trustcode: Warns TrustCode to measure appropriate reliance (both over- and under-reliance) and confidence calibration, not just overreliance.

title: What large language models know and what people think they know
authors: Mark Steyvers; Heliodoro Tejeda; Aakriti Kumar; Catarina Belem; Sheer Karny; Xinyue Hu; Lukas W. Mayer; Padhraic Smyth
venue: Nature Machine Intelligence
objective: Measure the calibration gap between human confidence in LLM answers and model confidence.
methodology: Experiments with multiple-choice and short-answer questions.
main_findings: Users overestimate LLM accuracy with default explanations; longer explanations raised confidence without improving accuracy.
relevance_to_trustcode: Supports calibration and discrimination metrics; warns that adaptive (longer) beginner explanations could inflate confidence.

title: To Trust or to Think: Cognitive Forcing Functions Can Reduce Overreliance on AI in AI-assisted Decision-making
authors: Zana Buçinca; Maja Barbara Malaya; Krzysztof Z. Gajos
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
objective: Test cognitive forcing functions to reduce overreliance.
methodology: Experiment comparing 3 cognitive forcing designs vs simple XAI vs no-AI.
main_findings: Cognitive forcing reduced overreliance relative to simple XAI but received the least favourable subjective ratings.
relevance_to_trustcode: Design option for TrustCode (e.g., confidence elicitation before seeing verdict) and a usability trade-off to monitor.

title: Closing the Gap: A User Study on the Real-world Usefulness of AI-powered Vulnerability Detection & Repair in the IDE
authors: Benjamin Steenhoek; Kalpathy Sivaraman; Renata Saldivar Gonzalez; Yevhen Mohylevskyy; Roshanak Zilouchian Moghaddam; Wei Le
venue: 2025 IEEE/ACM 47th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
objective: Assess real-world usefulness of an IDE-integrated AI vulnerability detection and repair tool.
methodology: DeepVulGuard deployed with professional developers on their own projects; observation and interviews.
main_findings: Promising benchmark performance did not translate to practice: high false-positive rate and non-applicable fixes; users wanted more context and customisation.
relevance_to_trustcode: Warns that false positives erode trust — TrustCode must show uncertainty and include spurious-warning items in its benchmark.

title: A Study on Developer Behaviors for Validating and Repairing LLM-Generated Code Using Eye Tracking and IDE Actions
authors: Ningzhi Tang; Meng Chen; Zheng Ning; Aakash Bansal; Yu Huang; Collin McMillan; Toby Jia-Jun Li
venue: arXiv preprint
objective: Investigate how developers validate and repair Copilot-generated code and the effect of provenance awareness.
methodology: Lab study with IDE logs, eye tracking, workload assessment and interviews; provenance-informed vs uninformed groups.
dataset: Three software projects with Copilot-generated code
main_findings: Without explicit information developers often failed to identify LLM-origin code; validation strategies were similar, with frequent code/comment switching and delete-and-rewrite behaviour.
limitations_reviewer_assessed: Preprint version reviewed; provenance is the only manipulated signal.
future_research: Tool support for validation of LLM code.
relevance_to_trustcode: Methodological template (IDE logs, workload) for measuring verification behaviour.

title: Ivie: Lightweight Anchored Explanations of Just-Generated Code
authors: Litao Yan; Alyssa Hwang; Zhiyuan Wu; Andrew Head
venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
objective: Accelerate inspection of just-generated code via anchored in-situ explanations.
methodology: VS Code fork with LLM-generated explanations adjacent to code; lab comparison with a baseline code-understanding tool.
main_findings: Ivie improved understanding of generated code and was perceived as useful and low-distraction.
limitations_reviewer_assessed: Explanations are LLM-generated (can themselves be wrong); outcome is understanding, not decision correctness or calibration.
relevance_to_trustcode: Interaction pattern (in-situ explanation) TrustCode can borrow; but TrustCode grounds explanations in tool evidence.

title: Why don't software developers use static analysis tools to find bugs?
authors: Brittany Johnson; Yoonki Song; Emerson Murphy-Hill; Robert Bowdidge
venue: 2013 35th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
objective: Why developers don't use static analysis tools.
main_findings: False positives and poorly presented warnings are major barriers to static analysis use.
relevance_to_trustcode: Raw tool output is not usable evidence — TrustCode's explanation layer must translate it.

theme: T5 Quality & security of AI code
title: From Preventive to Reactive: How AI Coding Assistants Transform Developers' Security Awareness
authors: Faisal Haque Bappy; Tahrim Hossain; Sidratul Muntaher Meheraj; Annoor Sharara Akhand; Tasfia Tabassum; Tarannum Shaila Zaman; Raiful Hasan; Tariqul Islam
venue: arXiv preprint
objective: How AI coding assistants change developers' security awareness.
main_findings: Security thinking shifts from writing to reviewing (preventive to reactive); no participant specified security requirements in prompts.
future_research: Tool support for reactive security review.
relevance_to_trustcode: Reviewing AI code is now where security happens — supports TrustCode's review-time evidence.

theme: T5 Quality & security of AI code
title: Security Weaknesses of Copilot-Generated Code in GitHub Projects: An Empirical Study
authors: Yujia Fu; Peng Liang; Amjed Tahir; Zengyang Li; Mojtaba Shahin; Jiaxin Yu; Jinfu Chen
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
objective: Security weaknesses of AI-generated code in GitHub projects.
main_findings: 29.5% of Python and 24.2% of JavaScript snippets had security weaknesses across 43 CWE categories.
limitations_reviewer_assessed: Attribution of AI origin relies on project annotations.
relevance_to_trustcode: Justifies Python + JavaScript MVP and CWE-based security evidence.

theme: T5 Quality & security of AI code
title: Calibration and Correctness of Language Models for Code
authors: Claudio Spiess; David Gros; Kunal Suresh Pai; Michael Pradel; Md Rafiqul Islam Rabin; Amin Alipour; Susmit Jha; Prem Devanbu; Toufique Ahmed
venue: 2025 IEEE/ACM 47th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
objective: Evaluate calibration of code LLMs.
methodology: Calibration evaluation framework for code generation.
main_findings: Calibration of generative code models is a distinct problem; framework for measuring it.
relevance_to_trustcode: Distinguishes model calibration from human trust calibration — TrustCode targets the latter.

theme: T5 Quality & security of AI code
title: We Have a Package for You! A Comprehensive Analysis of Package Hallucinations by Code Generating LLMs
authors: Joseph Spracklen; Raveen Wijewickrama; A H M Nazmus Sakib; Anindya Maiti; Bimal Viswanath; Murtuza Jadliwala
venue: arXiv preprint
objective: Analyse package hallucinations in code LLMs.
methodology: 576,000 samples from 16 LLMs in Python and JavaScript.
main_findings: Hallucinated packages averaged at least 5.2% (commercial) and 21.7% (open-source models); 205,474 unique hallucinated names.
limitations_reviewer_assessed: arXiv version reviewed (reported published at USENIX Security 2025 — confirm).
relevance_to_trustcode: Justifies dependency-existence check as an evidence stage.

theme: T5 Quality & security of AI code
title: Is Stack Overflow Obsolete? An Empirical Study of the Characteristics of ChatGPT Answers to Stack Overflow Questions
authors: Samia Kabir; David N. Udo-Imeh; Bonan Kou; Tianyi Zhang
venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
objective: Characterise ChatGPT answers to programming questions.
methodology: Analysis of 517 SO questions + linguistic analysis + user study.
main_findings: 52% of answers contained incorrect information; participants overlooked misinformation 39% of the time, partly due to well-articulated style.
relevance_to_trustcode: Fluent, confident text masks errors — supports evidence-first presentation.

theme: T5 Quality & security of AI code
title: Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation
authors: Jiawei Liu; Chunqiu Steven Xia; Yuyao Wang; Lingming Zhang
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36
objective: Rigorously evaluate functional correctness of LLM code.
main_findings: Augmented tests caught much previously undetected wrong code, reducing pass@k by up to 19.3-28.9%.
relevance_to_trustcode: Key fact: passing tests ≠ correct — TrustCode must show 'not tested' and coverage limits. Candidate benchmark source.

theme: T5 Quality & security of AI code
title: Asleep at the Keyboard? Assessing the Security of GitHub Copilot’s Code Contributions
authors: Hammond Pearce; Baleegh Ahmad; Benjamin Tan; Brendan Dolan-Gavitt; Ramesh Karri
venue: 2022 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
objective: Assess security of Copilot code contributions.
main_findings: Approximately 40% of generated programs were vulnerable.
relevance_to_trustcode: Motivates security evidence stage (Semgrep, CWE mapping).

title: From Generic to Personalized: Exploring Persona-Aware Code Review Explanations
authors: Shamse Tasnim Cynthia; Ratnadira Widyasari; Banani Roy; Italo Santos; David Lo
venue: arXiv preprint
objective: Explore persona-aware code review explanations.
main_findings: Preferred explanation styles vary by problem-solving style, experience and role; developers valued depth, learning support, practical suggestions and risk awareness over conciseness.
relevance_to_trustcode: Supports adaptation; also warns that adaptation must be balanced with clarity and trust.

title: Understanding user mental models in AI-driven code completion tools: Insights from an elicitation study
authors: Giuseppe Desolda; Andrea Esposito; Francesco Greco; Cesare Tucci; Paolo Buono; Antonio Piccinno
venue: International Journal of Human-Computer Studies
objective: Elicit developers' mental models of AI code completion tools.
main_findings: Developers need customisation of activation, display, granularity and explanation content.
limitations_reviewer_assessed: Elicitation; proof-of-concept not evaluated for calibration.
relevance_to_trustcode: Supports user-controlled adaptation of explanation content.

title: Investigating Explainability of Generative AI for Code through Scenario-based Design
authors: Jiao Sun; Q. Vera Liao; Michael Muller; Mayank Agarwal; Stephanie Houde; Kartik Talamadupula; Justin D. Weisz
venue: 27th International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces
objective: Elicit explainability needs for generative AI for code.
main_findings: Identified explainability needs and proposed 4 types of XAI features for GenAI for code.
relevance_to_trustcode: Grounds explanation content design.

title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
authors: Joel Becker; Nate Rush; Elizabeth Barnes; David Rein
venue: arXiv preprint
objective: RCT of early-2025 AI tools on experienced OSS developer productivity.
main_findings: Allowing AI increased completion time by 19%, despite developers believing it reduced time by 20%.
relevance_to_trustcode: Perception-performance gap: self-reports are unreliable — TrustCode must use behavioural measures.

title: Measures for explainable AI: Explanation goodness, user satisfaction, mental models, curiosity, trust, and human-AI performance
authors: Robert R. Hoffman; Shane T. Mueller; Gary Klein; Jordan Litman
venue: Frontiers in Computer Science
objective: Measures for XAI evaluation.
main_findings: Scales for explanation goodness, satisfaction, mental models, curiosity, trust/reliance, and work-system performance.
relevance_to_trustcode: Explanation satisfaction + trust instruments.

title: Foundations for an Empirically Determined Scale of Trust in Automated Systems
authors: Jiun-Yin Jian; Ann M. Bisantz; Colin G. Drury
venue: International Journal of Cognitive Ergonomics
objective: Empirically derived trust-in-automation scale.
main_findings: 12-item trust-in-automated-systems scale.
relevance_to_trustcode: Candidate attitudinal trust instrument.

title: Humans and Automation: Use, Misuse, Disuse, Abuse
authors: Raja Parasuraman; Victor Riley
venue: Human Factors: The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society
objective: Use, misuse, disuse, abuse of automation.
main_findings: Defines misuse (over-reliance) and disuse (under-reliance).
relevance_to_trustcode: Defines over/under-reliance constructs.

title: Development of NASA-TLX (Task Load Index): Results of Empirical and Theoretical Research
authors: Sandra G. Hart; Lowell E. Staveland
venue: Advances in Psychology
objective: Development of NASA-TLX.
main_findings: Six-subscale workload instrument.
relevance_to_trustcode: Workload measure (RQ3).

title: VERIFICATION OF FORECASTS EXPRESSED IN TERMS OF PROBABILITY
authors: GLENN W. BRIER
venue: Monthly Weather Review
objective: Scoring probabilistic forecasts.
main_findings: Defines the Brier score.
relevance_to_trustcode: Calibration metric for confidence judgements.

theme: T1 Interaction with AI code assistants
title: Developer Needs and Feasible Features for AI Assistants in IDEs
authors: Agnia Sergeyuk; Ekaterina Koshchenko; Ilya Zakharov; Timofey Bryksin; Maliheh Izadi
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/ACM 48th International Conference on Software Engineering: Software Engineering in Practice
objective: Identify developer needs and feasible features for in-IDE AI assistants.
main_findings: Five need areas incl. interaction, customisation and simplifying skill building.
relevance_to_trustcode: Industry demand for customisation/interaction support.

theme: T1 Interaction with AI code assistants
title: How Developers Interact with AI: A Taxonomy of Human-AI Collaboration in Software Engineering
authors: Christoph Treude; Marco A. Gerosa
venue: 2025 IEEE/ACM Second International Conference on AI Foundation Models and Software Engineering (Forge)
objective: Taxonomy of developer-AI interaction types.
